memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now his brothers had gone to graze their father's flocks near Shechem, and Israel said to Joseph, 'As you know, your brothers are grazing the flocks near Shechem. Come, I am going to send you to them.' 'Very well,' he replied. So he said to him, 'Go and see if all is well with your brothers and with the flocks, and bring word back to me.' Then he sent him off from the Valley of Hebron. When Joseph arrived at Shechem," - Gen 37:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob sends Joseph on an errand to check on his brothers: "Go and see if all is well." Joseph's response is simple and immediate: "Very well." He knows his brothers resent him, yet he obeys his father without argument and sets off on the long journey to find them.

There is quiet faithfulness in that little word, "Very well." Joseph did not know that this obedient errand would lead to a pit, to slavery, to years of hardship. He simply obeyed the word given to him and went. Faithfulness often means saying yes to God without seeing where the road will lead.

This is a picture worth pondering. A beloved son, sent by his father to his brothers who did not love him — going willingly, in obedience. It quietly foreshadows a greater Son, sent by His Father into a world that would reject Him, who came saying, "I have come to do your will" (Heb 10:7).

God still sends His people on errands whose outcomes we cannot see. Sometimes obedience leads to blessing we expected; sometimes it leads through hardship we never imagined. Either way, our call is the same as Joseph's — to say, "Very well," and go. Will you obey the Father's sending, even when you cannot see the road ahead?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I obey God's leading even when I cannot see where it leads?
2. What "errand" is God sending me on that requires simple trust?
3. How does Joseph's willing obedience point me to Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me Joseph's ready "Very well" when You send me, even when I cannot see the road ahead. Help me to obey in faith, trusting the Father who sends me. Amen.
